findings.claim: setupWcDappsTx's promise rejection is only logged with console.error, which Maestro cannot observe; if storePrivateKey fails on a simulator due to biometrics/keychain issues, the flow proceeds to synthTxRequest and later fails with a confusing symptom that has no direct pointer back to the setup failure.

The setup failure should be surfaced as a marker (e.g. e2e-wc-setup-failed) via walletKitE2eState so flows can assertNotVisible it before proceeding, mirroring the existing rejectSessionCalled/lastRequestResponse side-channels.

The useEffect has no dependency array, so it runs on every render since hashes = Object.keys(outstanding) produces a fresh array each render; it should depend on outstanding, or the ref update should be computed via useMemo on outstanding instead.

Object.keys(outstanding) order is insertion order, so treating the last key as the newest is not guaranteed by object key semantics; a comment tying this invariant to the one-outstanding-tx-per-test flow contract would prevent future readers from assuming ordering is guaranteed.

installProposeFetchMock captures global.fetch at install time and never restores it; if Jest test isolation unhooks or swaps global.fetch between suites, a second installProposeFetchMock() call returns early due to the module-scoped installed flag, silently leaving the interceptor uninstalled from the new fetch.

The install-once, per-Metro-lifetime contract should be documented explicitly, or an uninstallProposeFetchMock() function should be exposed so tests running against the module in isolation can rebind.

The wei jitter formula combines Date.now() with an incrementing counter to avoid collisions, but two flows starting within the same wall-clock millisecond and hitting the same jitterSeq value across module reloads could theoretically still collide.

A raw private key is committed to the repository; even though it is a throwaway Sepolia-only key, committing raw keys attracts secret-scanner attention and creates false positives on downstream forks, so it should be gated behind an env var or documented as intentionally public.

The assertVisible selector text: 'Send' matches any UI element containing the word 'Send' (action, button, or tab), so it should use a stable testID on the queued tx row or a more tightly scoped text match.
The assertVisible selector text: '.*0\.001.*' can match multiple UI surfaces that render this fixture value, making the assertion insufficiently specific.

extendedWaitUntil timeout values (e.g. 30000 for sign, 10000 for sheet) are duplicated across all five new Maestro flows, so a shared constants.yml or Maestro env variables would let a CI-slow timeout bump be made in one place instead of many.
